[element-ics-desc]
=== `<ics-desc>` ICS Code Description

The name/title/description of a decimal code from the International Classification for Standards. The element <<element-ics,`<ics>`>> holds the decimal number while this `<ics-desc>` element holds the text that names/defines the decimal code.

#### Usage/Remarks
##### Code versus Code and Description

When NISO STS was being designed, it became clear that some standards organizations felt that only numeric ICS codes should be stored in the XML, while other organizations wished to record both the decimal code and the natural language expansion (description/name/title) of that code. So NISO STS has been designed to be used either way: ICS decimal codes can be stored in the <<element-ics,`<ics>`>> element in the standard’s metadata. Alternatively, an <<element-ics-wrap,`<ics-wrap>`>> grouping element can be used to hold both an ICS decimal code (<<element-ics,`<ics>`>>) and the expansion of that code (<<element-ics-desc,`<ics-desc>`>>). The <<element-ics-desc,`<ics-desc>`>> element can take a language attribute (<<attribute-xml-lang,`@xml:lang`>>) to name the language of the description/name/title.

#### Related Elements

NISO STS standards metadata describe key concepts that are _not ICS terms_ as either keywords (inside the <<element-kwd-group,`<kwd-group>`>> element) or as subjects (inside <<element-subj-group,`<subj-group>`>>). ICS codes use their own ICS-specific elements: <<element-ics-wrap,`<ics-wrap>`>>, <<element-ics,`<ics>`>>, and <<element-ics-desc,`<ics-desc>`>>.

#### Tagged Samples

#### ICS code with its description in German

[source,xml]
....
...
<nat-meta originator="SFS">
...
<secretariat>...</secretariat>
<ics-wrap>
<ics>13.310</ics>
<ics-desc xml:lang="de">Sicherheitstechnik</ics-desc>
</ics-wrap>
</nat-meta>
...
....
